elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against the covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2 states that Vendor shall defend Customer and its Affiliates against any third-party claim within the listed categories.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against the covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2 states that Vendor shall indemnify Customer and its Affiliates against any third-party claim within the listed categories.

elements.element: Covered claims must include third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(a) covers allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Covered claims must include third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(b) expressly covers Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: Covered claims must include third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(c) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, which operatively covers a Vendor-caused Customer Data breach.

elements.element: Covered claims must include third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(d) expressly covers Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require prompt notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 20.3 requires the indemnified Party to give prompt written notice of the claim.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give the indemnifying Party control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 20.3 provides that the indemnifying Party shall control the defence.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require reasonable cooperation from the indemnified Party.
elements.evidence: Section 20.3 requires the indemnified Party to provide reasonable cooperation.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover claims relating to Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1 limits the content trigger to Customer's content provided to the Services.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover claims arising from Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1 expressly includes Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must contain no triggers other than Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The former indemnity for every claim relating to Customer's use was narrowed to the two stated triggers, with no additional trigger retained.

elements.element: Vendor must provide an intellectual-property indemnity to Customer for third-party infringement claims involving the Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(a) requires Vendor to defend and indemnify Customer for third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims resulting from Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for modifications made by Customer appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims resulting from combinations with other products, services, or materials.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims resulting from compliance with Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specifications exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP remedies must include procuring the right for Customer to continue using the affected item.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no procurement-of-rights remedy.

elements.element: The Vendor IP remedies must include modifying the affected item to make it non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: The Vendor IP remedies must include replacing the affected item with a non-infringing alternative.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: The Vendor IP remedies must include a refund remedy.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No operative three-times-annual-fees cap is shown; the Section 21 heading alone does not establish such a cap.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the preferred position by adding the specified Vendor indemnity, notice/control/cooperation procedure, and narrowed Customer indemnity. It does not satisfy the fallback because the required IP exclusions, remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent. The substantive changes are targeted and preserve the surrounding terms. Drafting quality is reduced because Sections 20.2 and 20.3 appear after the Section 21 heading, creating a significant numbering and placement defect, and because “Customer's content provided to the Services” is less precise than “content provided by Customer.”
